headlines.title: Adobe $47.5 Billion in Online Spend Expected Over Black Friday + Cyber Monday
headlines.summary: How strong will online shopping demand be during the critical holiday shopping season? In this NYSE Live interview, Vivek Pandya, Director of Digital Insights at Adobe (NASDAQ: ADBE), discusses Adobe's latest holiday shopping forecast, consumer spending trends, discount expectations, and the growing role of artificial intelligence in e-commerce. Ashley Mastronardi spoke with Pandya about Cyber Week spending, Black Friday and Cyber Monday trends, online shopping behavior, retailer promotions, and how AI is reshaping the customer journey. A major theme throughout the conversation is holiday spending strength. According to Adobe's latest analysis, Cyber Week is expected to generate approximately $47.5 billion in online spending, representing a significant increase from the prior year. The interview also explores Adobe's broader holiday shopping outlook, which forecasts approximately $275.1 billion in total online holiday spending as consumers continue embracing e-commerce and digital retail experiences. Another key topic is consumer responsiveness to discounts. Adobe has observed strong activity throughout November as shoppers increasingly take advantage of early holiday promotions and seasonal sales. The conversation further examines how spending accelerates dramatically during the period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, making it one of the most important shopping windows of the year. A significant focus of the discussion is promotional activity across major retail categories. The interview also highlights expectations for strong discounts in categories such as apparel, toys, electronics, and other popular holiday gift segments. Another major theme is consumer value-seeking behavior. Shoppers continue prioritizing competitive pricing, promotions, loyalty programs, and discount opportunities as they navigate the holiday season. The discussion also explores the impact of lower fuel prices and how consumers are balancing everyday necessities with discretionary holiday purchases. Additionally, Pandya discusses changes in purchasing behavior related to essential goods. The conversation further examines how consumers are increasingly using holiday promotions to stock up on household necessities and core products in addition to traditional gift purchases. Another key topic is artificial intelligence and its growing influence on online shopping. The interview also highlights Adobe's findings that consumers are using AI-powered tools to discover products, compare prices, identify promotions, and make more informed purchasing decisions. A significant focus is AI-driven commerce. According to Adobe's research, users arriving at retailer websites through AI-enabled experiences are demonstrating higher conversion rates and stronger engagement compared with traditional traffic sources. The discussion further explores how AI is helping consumers narrow choices, identify value opportunities, and streamline the overall shopping journey. Another important theme is digital transformation in retail. Retailers continue investing in personalization, promotions, and data-driven customer experiences to gain market share during the holiday season. Looking ahead, Adobe expects consumers to remain highly engaged throughout Cyber Week, with discount-driven demand, AI-assisted shopping, and value-focused purchasing behavior supporting online sales growth. Throughout the discussion, Pandya shares insights on e-commerce, holiday shopping, online retail, Cyber Monday, Black Friday, consumer spending, artificial intelligence, digital marketing, retail trends, and shopping behavior. description: Adobe Inc. operates as a technology company worldwide. The Digital Media segment offers products and services that enable individuals, teams, and enterprises to create, publish, and promote content. This segment serves photographers, video editors, graphic and experience designers, game developers, content creators, students, marketers, business owners, knowledge workers, and consumers. The Digital Experience segment provides an integrated platform; and products, services, and solutions that enable brands and businesses to create, manage, execute, measure, monetize, and optimize customer experiences from analytics to commerce. This segment serves marketers, advertisers, agencies, publishers, merchandisers, merchants, web analysts, data scientists, developers, and executives across the C-suite. The Publishing and Advertising segment offers e-learning, technical document publishing, web conferencing, document and forms platform, web application development, printing, and Adobe Advertising solutions. It also provides consulting, training, customer management, technical support, and learning services. The company offers its solutions to enterprise customers, and businesses and consumers; and licenses its products to end-user customers through app stores and website at adobe.com. It markets and distributes its products through distributors, retailers, software developers, mobile app stores, systems integrators, independent software vendors, value-added resellers, and original equipment and hardware manufacturers. The company also provides an online visibility management and content marketing software-as-a-service platform. The company has a strategic alliance with HUMAIN for the development of generative AI models and AI-powered applications. The company was formerly known as Adobe Systems Incorporated and changed its name to Adobe Inc. in October 2018. Adobe Inc. was founded in 1982 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
